text: ok now you need to give those pieces the same placement capabilities. for example a normal floor i can paint it out as a grid for placement. but i cant do that with my custom floor piece. no reason other than poor planning
resolution: Gave cooked wall/floor pieces the same drag-paint placement as the built-ins. A built-in floor fills a dragged rectangle with a grid and a built-in wall paints a line, but a cooked floor/wall could only rotate on drag: the capability gate (paintKindOf in IsoAuthor) read GAME_BUILD.catalog.get(id).kind, which is 'prop' for every cooked mesh substrate, so it returned null. Fix: added catalogPieceFamily(id) to the catalog (the effective build family of any id — a cooked wall/floor resolves to 'wall'/'floor' via its buildPlacement.pieceKind, built-ins are their own kind), exposed it as GAME_BUILD.catalog.family, and paintKindOf now reads the family. So a custom floor grid-fills a drag and a custom wall paints a line, pitched to the cooked piece's measured footprint, identical to the built-ins; single-click grid/edge snap already worked via the entry's snap field. Regression test in cookedPiece.test.ts (catalogPieceFamily: cooked floor→floor, free prop→prop, built-in floor→floor): 12/12 pass. TSX/TS, hot-reloads in rjit dev.
